title: Differential Regression Testing for REST APIs
authors: Patrice Godefroid, Daniel Lehmann, Marina Polishchuk
central_claim: Differential testing across 17 Azure networking API versions (2016-2019) found 14 regressions: 5 in specifications, 9 in the services.
cite_claim: Service regressions occur while the specification is held fixed; in Azure all 9 were response properties the spec did not declare, so a spec diff alone misses them.
location: Abstract; Sec. 4.3 Found Regressions - Overview; Table 2
quote: detected 14 regressions in total, 5 of those in the official API specifications and 9 regressions in the services themselves.
relevance: Deep-read. Closest prior method to response-level drift detection. Note its 9 service regressions were additive, mostly benign, structural diffs, not wrong values.

title: A First Look at the Deprecation of RESTful APIs: An Empirical Study
authors: Jerin Yasmin, Yuan Tian, Jinqiu Yang
central_claim: Of 251 RESTful API versions that introduced breaking changes, 87.3% did not deprecate anything in the prior version; only 3 of 219 APIs used proactive runtime signals.
cite_claim: Web API providers rarely announce breaking changes through the spec or at runtime, so clients cannot rely on deprecation metadata.
quote: 87.3% of RESTful API versions that introduced breaking changes do not provide any deprecation information in the previous version.
relevance: Deep-read. Quantifies the 'no warning' premise on 2,224 OpenAPI specs (APIs.guru). Spec-level only: cannot see behavioral drift.

title: Breaking changes (GitHub REST API docs)
central_claim: GitHub defines removing/renaming fields and removing enum values as breaking; adding fields, adding enum values and optional params as additive.
cite_claim: A major provider ships enum additions in every supported API version as non-breaking, so closed-enum clients can silently misroute new values.
location: Page body: breaking vs additive lists
quote: Adding enum values
relevance: Provider-side definition of what may change without a version bump.

title: Upgrade your integration (Stripe docs)
central_claim: Unpinned requests use the account default API version; older SDK majors (stripe-python <v6, stripe-node <v12) used the account default.
cite_claim: For older Stripe SDKs, a Dashboard API-version upgrade changes response structure for the same client code.
location: Sections 'Specify the API version in your SDK' (Python, Node subsections)
quote: Versions of stripe-python before v6 use your account's default API version.
relevance: Silent version switch as a drift trigger (API-16).

title: 2022-11-15 release (Stripe changelog)
central_claim: Version 2022-11-15 removed PaymentIntent.charges, stopped auto-expanding Charge refunds, and added decline codes, each labelled Breaking.
cite_claim: Stripe classifies new decline-code values as breaking, unlike GitHub's 'adding enum values is additive' rule.
quote: Removes the `charges` attribute from the `PaymentIntent` object
relevance: API-11, API-12, API-13; evidence of provider disagreement on enum additions.

title: Supported currencies: special cases (Stripe docs)
central_claim: ISK and UGX are zero-decimal currencies but must be sent as two-decimal values; HUF/TWD payouts must be divisible by 100.
cite_claim: Real 100x unit traps exist in a major payments API and are documented only in prose.
quote: ISK transitioned to a zero-decimal currency, but backward compatibility requires you to represent it as a two-decimal value
relevance: Closest real analog to seeded D1 (API-14).

title: Search (Stripe docs): data freshness and data mismatches
central_claim: Search is eventually consistent (normally under 1 minute) and can return objects whose current status does not match the status filter.
cite_claim: Read-after-write through a search endpoint is explicitly unsafe in Stripe; correct postconditions must use retrieve/list.
quote: Don't use search for read-after-write flows (for example, searching immediately after a charge is made)

title: API versioning (Shopify docs)
central_claim: Requests to retired versions are answered by the oldest accessible stable version, signalled in a response header.
cite_claim: A pinned client can silently receive a newer API version's behavior when its version retires.
location: Section on unsupported versions / fall forward
quote: Shopify falls forward and responds using the oldest accessible stable version.

title: REST API endpoints for commits (GitHub docs)
central_claim: Get a commit paginates files beyond 300 (to 3000); Compare is limited to 250 commits without paging params.
cite_claim: GitHub silently caps list sizes inside single-object responses; only Link headers reveal more data.
location: Get a commit (note); Compare two commits (note)
quote: the returned list is limited to 250 commits

title: REST API endpoints for repository contents (GitHub docs)
central_claim: For 1-100 MB files only raw/object media types are supported; object returns empty content with encoding none; directories capped at 1,000 files.
cite_claim: A 200 response can carry an empty content string for a non-empty file.
location: Get repository content: file size limits
quote: the content field will be an empty string and the encoding field will be "none".

title: REST API endpoints for search (GitHub docs)
central_claim: Search queries that time out return partial matches with incomplete_results=true; up to 1,000 results per search.
cite_claim: Partial results arrive as HTTP 200, flagged only by a body field.
quote: the API returns the matches that were already found prior to the timeout

title: Upcoming changes to GitHub Events API payloads
central_claim: On 2025-10-07 GitHub removed author_association and other costly fields from several event payloads.
cite_claim: A major API removed payload fields in place with the endpoint still returning 200, announced only in a changelog post.
quote: The `author_association` field will be removed from multiple event types

title: Rate limit changes for non-Marketplace apps
central_claim: From 2025-05-29, new non-Marketplace installs get conversations.history/replies at 1 request/minute with limit max/default 15.
cite_claim: A provider cut page size and rate for one class of apps overnight; single-page readers silently see fewer messages.
quote: The maximum and default for the `limit` parameter has been reduced to 15 objects.

title: Gateway: Message Content Intent (Discord docs)
central_claim: Without the privileged intent, content/embeds/attachments/components/poll arrive empty except in DMs, mentions and own messages.
cite_claim: Configuration-dependent empty values are delivered as normal payloads.
quote: Apps without the intent will receive empty values in fields that contain user-inputted content

title: Initial support for pomelo migration (discord.py commit df01db34; v2.3.0 notes)
central_claim: discord.py v2.3.0 changed User.__str__ to drop discriminators for migrated users, detected by discriminator == '0'.
cite_claim: A value-semantics change (discriminator '0') required a client code fix with no schema change.
quote: Update __str__ for User to drop discriminators if the user has been migrated.

title: Twitch API change log
central_claim: Get Users view_count was kept but serves stale data; tag_ids was kept but always returns an empty array.
cite_claim: Providers deprecate by keeping a field and degrading its value, which passes any schema check.
location: Entries on view_count deprecation and tag_ids deprecation (2023-02-28)
quote: The response continues to include the field; however, it contains stale data.

title: YouTube Data API revision history
central_claim: On 2021-12-15 statistics.dislikeCount became private.
cite_claim: A widely used field disappeared from public responses on a date-stamped revision.
quote: the video resource's statistics.dislikeCount property is now private.

title: Telegram Bot API reference (User, Chat)
central_claim: User and chat ids may exceed 32 significant bits; store as 64-bit integer or double.
cite_claim: Identifier range exceeds common 32-bit types without any type change.
quote: This number may have more than 32 significant bits

title: PyPI JSON API
central_claim: The release-specific endpoint omits the releases key; downloads is always -1 on both endpoints.
cite_claim: Sentinel values (-1) and removed keys are documented only in prose and pass type checks.
quote: downloads: this key is always -1 and should not be used.

title: Deprecation notice and migration guide for major changes to Jira Cloud REST APIs to improve user privacy
central_claim: username/userKey removed from Jira Cloud REST responses in favor of accountId (deprecation from 2018-10-01, removal scheduled 2019-04-29).
cite_claim: A large API removed user identifier fields across endpoints over a six-month window.
quote: the response will not include a username and userkey

title: Add enhanced_search_issues API for Jira Cloud using new search/jql endpoint (pycontribs/jira #2326)
central_claim: The client added nextPageToken pagination and approximate counts because Atlassian was removing the old search API.
cite_claim: Pagination contract changes in a provider forced client rewrites (search -> search/jql).
quote: Atlassian will remove support for the old search API on May 1, 2025.

title: REST API: pagination response headers (GitLab docs)
central_claim: For queries over 10,000 records GitLab omits x-total, x-total-pages and rel=last.
cite_claim: Pagination metadata disappears above a size threshold.
quote: if a query returns more than 10,000 records, GitLab doesn't return the following headers

title: Implement shared drive support (Google Drive API)
central_claim: files.list excludes shared-drive items unless includeItemsFromAllDrives (and supportsAllDrives) are set; files.list may return fewer than pageSize and can flag incompleteSearch.
cite_claim: A list call can omit whole classes of results with a 200 response depending on flags.
quote: If not present or set to false, then shared drive items are not returned.

title: Place Details (Places API legacy) (Google Maps Platform docs)
central_claim: permanently_closed is deprecated; use business_status (OPERATIONAL, CLOSED_TEMPORARILY, CLOSED_PERMANENTLY).
cite_claim: Deprecated boolean flags can be replaced by enums; readers of the old flag see 'not closed'.
quote: permanently_closed is deprecated.

title: Upgrade guide: 2025-09-03 (Notion API)
central_claim: Once a database gains a second data source, older-version integrations fail on database calls and silently get no search results for it.
cite_claim: User actions in the product can make an unchanged integration's search silently incomplete.
location: Section on behavior for older API versions
quote: existing connections will not see any search results for that database

title: Paging Microsoft Graph data in your app
central_claim: Pages may have zero or more results; $top may be ignored; custom headers like ConsistencyLevel are not carried to next pages; @odata.count only on page 1.
cite_claim: Large APIs document paging behaviors that defeat naive single-page or fixed-size assumptions.
location: How paging works; bullet list of paging behaviors
quote: The requested page size might be ignored, it might default to the maximum page size for that API

title: Graph API v2.4 changelog: Declarative Fields
central_claim: From v2.4 GET requests return only explicitly requested fields (e.g. /me/feed no longer includes likes and comments by default).
cite_claim: A default-response change removed fields for clients that did not enumerate them.
quote: Nodes and Edges in v2.4 requires that you explicitly request the field(s) you need for your GET requests.

title: Handling stop reasons (Claude API docs)
central_claim: Seven stop_reason values incl. pause_turn, refusal, model_context_window_exceeded; refusal is a normal HTTP 200.
cite_claim: New enum values carry safety- and control-flow meaning yet arrive as successful responses.
quote: Safety classifiers return this stop reason as a normal HTTP 200 response, not an error.

central_claim: Anthropic's refusal stop_reason was missing from LiteLLM's finish-reason map and fell through to 'stop'.
cite_claim: A gateway translated a safety refusal into a normal completion because of a default branch for unknown enum values.

title: fix(bedrock): avoid double-counting cache tokens in Anthropic Messages streaming usage (BerriAI/litellm #25517)
central_claim: Bedrock streaming usage was rewritten so cache tokens were counted twice, roughly doubling reported prompt tokens and spend.
cite_claim: Accounting-unit mismatches between provider surfaces silently double costs.
quote: cached requests could report roughly 2x the real prompt token total and inflated spend.

title: Anthropic cost calculations are incorrect with prompt caching (BerriAI/litellm #9812; fix #9838)
central_claim: cache_creation_input_tokens were charged twice, nearly doubling computed cost.
cite_claim: New provider usage fields were mis-accounted by a widely used gateway.
quote: This results in a cost calculation that is almost double

title: Negative text_tokens in prompt_tokens_details when image caching is used with Gemini (BerriAI/litellm #18750; fix #18768)
central_claim: Gemini modality token breakdown led LiteLLM to report negative text token counts.
cite_claim: Range invariants (counts >= 0) catch real accounting bugs.
quote: returns negative values for text_tokens in prompt_tokens_details

title: commit.files result has a limit of 300 files (PyGithub #1745); Make Commit.files return PaginatedList (#2939)
central_claim: PyGithub returned at most 300 files per commit from 2020 until the 2024 fix that follows pagination.
cite_claim: A popular SDK silently truncated data for about 3.5 years despite a documented provider limit.
quote: I have a large commit that has 926 changed files ... I got 300.
relevance: Deep-read. API-01; PyGithub tests use recorded ReplayData, so offline replay is feasible.

title: github_issue_write silently drops labels when caller lacks AddLabelsToLabelable permission (#3160); fix #3195
central_claim: GitHub accepted issue create/update but dropped labels; the MCP server reported success until it compared requested vs returned labels.
cite_claim: The official GitHub MCP server shipped a read-after-write style postcondition to catch a silent partial write.
location: Issue #3160 'Describe the bug'; PR #3195 Summary/What changed
quote: Detect when GitHub accepts an issue create or update request but omits requested labels
relevance: Deep-read. API-04; direct precedent for fiks's postcondition contracts.

central_claim: An MCP tool returned only the first ~30 reviews with no pagination.
cite_claim: Pagination truncation occurs in a production MCP server, not only in seeded benches.
quote: only returns the first page of results (~30 reviews)

title: get_file_contents fails on every file over 1 MB (#3417); fix #3419

cite_claim: Empty-value responses from GitHub reach MCP tools.
quote: The Contents API returns files over 1 MB with `"content": ""` and `"encoding": "none"`

title: Price Repair (yfinance docs)
central_claim: Yahoo sometimes mixes currency units so prices are 100x wrong; yfinance detects and repairs them statistically and flags repaired rows.
cite_claim: Upstream unit drift (100x) occurs in a real data API and a popular wrapper maintains a hand-built runtime detector for it.
quote: Sometimes Yahoo mixes up currencies e.g. $/cents or £/pence. So some prices are 100x wrong.

quote: is truncated to 140 characters, as needed.

title: Structured Outputs: refusals (OpenAI API docs)
central_claim: Refusals appear as a separate refusal content item that does not necessarily follow the requested schema.
cite_claim: Schema-conformant output is not guaranteed even with strict schemas; new content types must be handled.
quote: the API response will include a new field called `refusal`

title: Message resource (Twilio docs)
central_claim: price is populated only after the message is sent/received; status moves asynchronously (queued -> sent -> delivered).
cite_claim: Fields read immediately after a write can be null or non-final.
quote: The price is populated after the message has been sent/received

title: Amazon S3 Strong Consistency
central_claim: S3 now provides strong read-after-write and list consistency; previously eventual.
cite_claim: Read-after-write anomalies were a documented property of a major API for years.
quote: Amazon S3 now delivers strong read-after-write and list consistency automatically for all applications.

title: Introducing some changes to our Web API (Spotify for Developers blog)
central_claim: From 2024-11-27, new and development-mode apps lose access to several endpoints and to 30-second preview URLs in multi-get responses.
cite_claim: Field-level restrictions keyed on app status change response content for some clients only.
location: Post body: list of restricted endpoints and functionality
quote: new Web API use cases will no longer be able to access or use the following endpoints and functionality

title: Hyrum's Law
central_claim: With enough users, all observable behaviors of a system will be depended on by somebody.
cite_claim: Additive or 'non-breaking' provider changes still break some clients, because clients depend on observed, not promised, behavior.
quote: all observable behaviors of your system will be depended on by somebody.
relevance: Framing for why provider-classified non-breaking changes break wrappers.

title: TolerantReader
central_claim: Service consumers should be as tolerant as possible when reading data.
cite_claim: The standard engineering advice (tolerate unknown/missing data) is the same mechanism that turns drift into silent wrong data (e.g. default branches).
quote: be as tolerant as possible when reading data from a service
relevance: Strongest design counter-position; fiks reconciles it by making tolerance observable (receipts).
